newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu to attend Gabon talks Wednesday - CNN.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu to attend Gabon talks Wednesday - CNN.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, under pressure to resign as rebels close in on Kinshasa, will leave the capital for talks in Gabon on Wednesday but intends to return, Cable News Network reported on Tuesday.

A senior presidential official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters he was checking the report but stressed that there was no question of Mobutu fleeing as Laurent Kabila rebels advanced on the city.
"The president has made it clear that he is not going to flee," he said.
CNN, quoting Western diplomats in Kinshasa, said Mobutu would fly to Gabon's capital Libreville on Wednesday to attend a Great Lake regional summit with the president of Gabon, Congo and Togo.
Mobutu reportedly intended to return on Friday, CNN added.

The aide said that Mobutu, Kabila and South Africa's Nelson Mandela had agreed at inconclusive weekend talks on a South African ship in Congo's port of Pointe Noire that there would be follow-up talks this week prior to another peace summit.
"It was agreed that the follow-up to the meeting on the Outeniqua would be held by Wednesday," he said, adding that the follow-up meeting was to be in Libreville.

Kabila has said his rebels are within 85 km (50 miles) of the capital of five million people. He has demanded that Mobutu, who has dominated Zaire since seizing power in 1965, stand down and transfer power to the rebels immediately.
